blocked.what: of all shot attempts, this many were blocked by a body (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games)

neverReachedTheGoalie.what: of all shot attempts, this many never reached the goalie — blocked or missed (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games)

reachedTheGoalie.what: of all shot attempts, this many reached the goalie (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games)

saveFraction.what: of the shots a goalie actually faced, this many were saved — an empty-net goal is not among them, and neither is a shootout attempt (n counts SHOTS FACED, not games, and is NOT goals + shots on goal)

moreAttemptsLost.what: the team with more shot attempts lost

moreFaceoffsLost.what: the team that won more face-offs lost

moreLevelControlLost.what: the team that controlled play while the score was tied lost

moreShotsOnGoalLost.what: the team with more shots on goal lost

endZone.what: shot attempts taken before the next whistle after an end-zone face-off, counted for the team attacking that end and for the team defending it, out of every end-zone face-off (n counts FACE-OFFS, not games). The defending team’s attempts are shots at the FAR end — what getting the puck out and back up the ice looks like — so the pair says how strongly play tends to stay where the whistle put it, and says nothing about the contest at the line itself, which leaves no event in the record.

faceoffRun.what: the shot attempts in the run of play a face-off opens, until the next whistle: for the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and later attempt, how many the team that won the face-off took (w) out of all (n); and how many runs saw a shot attempt at all, by the winner, and by the loser (n counts FACE-OFFS)

hits.what: whether a team that lands more hits in a game also takes fewer shot attempts in it, measured two ways over every game we hold (n counts GAMES). The first is how strongly the two move together, where a negative number means they run opposite; the second asks the same thing without any assumption about the shape of the data — the share of games in which the team with more hits had fewer attempts. Hits are counted by each home rink’s own crew, and the same teams are credited with more of them at home than away, so this measures the scorers as well as the play.

pace.what: shot attempts taken in one situation, out of the minutes played in that situation, scaled to sixty — so a power-play rate and an even-strength rate can be set beside each other (attempts counts ATTEMPTS and minutes counts MINUTES, neither counts games). The power play and the penalty kill are divided by the SAME minutes, counted once from each side, as are trailing and leading.

reviews.what: reviews of a goal across the archive, as counts: coach’s challenges, and how many the challenging coach won (the goal came off, or the team’s own goal was made to count); reviews the league started itself, and how many took the goal off.

runLength.what: each run of play, from a face-off to the next whistle: the events the replay numbers on the ice, and the seconds on the game clock; 3 in 4 runs end within p75 and 9 in 10 within p90 (n counts RUNS OF PLAY)

shift.what: how long a skater’s shift lasts, on average, in seconds: the seconds every skater spent on the ice, shift by shift, divided by the number of shifts (n counts SHIFTS, not games). Goaltenders are left out, since a goaltender’s shift is most of the game, and a shift the record gives no end for is left out rather than counted as nothing.

shooter.what: shot attempts split by the position the roster lists for the player who took them, and for each group what became of those attempts — blocked, on goal, missed, or a goal (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games). Position is what the roster says and not a judgement about where a player was standing, so a defenceman who has walked to the top of the circle is still counted as one.

whistles.what: how often play stops for each reason across the archive, as counts rather than as rates: penalties called, plays ruled offside, pucks iced, power plays begun, and the goals scored by each side during them. A power play is counted where the advantage CHANGES, so it is not the same thing as a penalty — one trip to the box can be two of them, and one ends early when a goal is scored.

corsi.what: shot attempts by both teams in one game, at all strengths (n counts GAMES, not events)

attempts.what: of the unblocked shot attempts whose location the feed records, this many were taken from inside the slot — within 33 ft of the attacking net, inside 22 ft of centre, and in front of the goal line (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games, and a blocked shot is excluded because the coordinate the feed records for one is the BLOCKER's, not the shooter's)

scoredFromInside.what: of the unblocked attempts taken from INSIDE the slot, this many were goals (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games, over the games carrying BOTH goal and attempt placement)

scoredFromOutside.what: of the unblocked attempts taken from OUTSIDE the slot, this many were goals (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games, over the games carrying BOTH goal and attempt placement)

slot.what: of the goals scored in play whose location the feed records, this many were taken from inside the slot — within 33 ft of the attacking net, inside 22 ft of centre, and in front of the goal line (n counts GOALS, not games, and excludes the shootout)
